title: Implement User 'Last Active' Timestamp and 'Consistent Learner' Achievement
description: EduPulse Live, an event-driven learning social network, aims to boost user engagement. The product team has proposed a new feature to track user activity and reward them for consistent participation. This task involves modifying multiple C-based microservices to implement this feature, requiring changes to the database, user authentication logic, event publishing, and notification consumption. The system's backend is a distributed architecture where services communicate via a Kafka-based event bus.

project_spec.name: EduPulse Live — Event-Driven Learning Social Network
project_spec.description:
EduPulse Live is an expert-level, event-driven social web platform written in C that turns every learning activity into a real-time social signal. Students, instructors, and institution admins interact through lessons, quizzes, live streams, and peer-review sessions that immediately propagate as events over a distributed message bus. Rather than polling for updates, client dashboards, progress trackers, and analytics widgets subscribe to course, user, and assessment channels; when an assignment is graded, a quiz is submitted, or a study group starts a video huddle, the corresponding micro-services publish events that instantly update engaged users, trigger adaptive content suggestions, or fire off micro-credential minting workflows.

The education emphasis is reflected in specialized services such as the “Adaptive Curriculum Engine,” “Peer-Feedback Orchestrator,” and “Accreditation Ledger,” all orchestrated via an event broker. Social interactions (likes, comments, study-buddy matching) are treated as first-class educational artefacts, enriching learner profiles and driving gamified progress mechanics. By combining Component Architecture, MVC for the web UI, a REST API façade, Authentication Middleware, and repository-backed domain entities, EduPulse Live scales to campus-wide deployments while remaining highly maintainable for curriculum engineers and DevOps teams.
dependencies: libwebsockets (full-duplex WebSocket support for live classrooms)
CivetWeb or Mongoose (embedded HTTP/REST server in C)
libpq (PostgreSQL driver) or MySQL C connector (database integration via ORM layer)
hiredis (Redis client for caching and session management)
rabbitmq-c (AMQP client for the message broker)
wolfSSL or mbedTLS (optional lightweight TLS for embedded builds)
libjwt (JSON Web Token generation/verification for user_authentication and social_login)
Cairo + librsvg (server-side SVG/PDF rendering for certificates)
libsass (server-side CSS preprocessing to support responsive_design templates)
